svg.title: Engines against our model, with and without its router bias
svg.desc: SGLang 0.5.23, stock bf16: 68.5% same top-1 as G5, 96.0% as G5 without its router bias; SGLang 0.5.23, stock fp16: 68.4% same top-1 as G5, 99.4% as G5 without its router bias; vLLM 0.33.0 bf16: 93.4% same top-1 as G5, 69.6% as G5 without its router bias; vLLM 0.33.0 fp16: 98.7% same top-1 as G5, 68.9% as G5 without its router bias; SGLang + diagnostic patch bf16: 93.0% same top-1 as G5, 69.1% as G5 without its router bias; SGLang + diagnostic patch fp16: 98.6% same top-1 as G5, 68.9% as G5 without its router bias; G5 itself, rounded bf16: 91.8% same top-1 as G5, 66.6% as G5 without its router bias; G5 itself, rounded fp16: 98.6% same top-1 as G5, 68.6% as G5 without its router bias
svg.text: OUR MODEL’S EXPORT · RANDOM WEIGHTS · 12 PROMPTS · 2,016 POSITIONS
Stock SGLang matches our model with the router bias removed
Same top-1 next token as G5 in fp32, one request at a time. Rounding moves both dots; dropping the bias swaps them.
vs our model (G5 fp32, as exported)
vs G5 with its router bias set to zero
fp16 shrinks the rounding noise, not the gap: stock SGLang’s distance from our model is a routing difference.
